guards.invariant: an in-flight primary turn never ends while no live watcher supervises this home
guards.source: state/<id>.status in-flight rows, state/.last-watcher-beat age, watcher lock owner
guards.trigger: in-flight task, source, check, or queued wake exists and no live watcher holds state/<id>.lock past the derived grace
guards.remedy: bin/fm-supervision-instructions.sh --repair-line (renders this home's arm command: claude bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh, codex bin/fm-watch-checkpoint.sh --seconds <n>, grok <grok_arm>, pi/omp in-editor arm tool)
guards.layer_note: Stop and turn-end hosts; the shared predicate lives in bin/fm-supervision-liveness-lib.sh

exemptions.case: branch actor does not present its own wake rows
exemptions.derivation: the supervision branch can act on nothing outside its grant, so a drain instruction would be wrong

guards.invariant: a fleet command warns when supervision is not live
guards.source: watcher lock, beacon age, per-actor pending wake rows
guards.trigger: a fleet mutation runs while the watcher is unhealthy or wake rows are pending for this actor
guards.remedy: bin/fm-supervision-instructions.sh --repair-line (renders the arm command for this harness and home)
guards.layer_note: shares the liveness predicate with turnend-supervision-block through bin/fm-supervision-liveness-lib.sh

guards.invariant: unread wake rows are drained before anything else
guards.source: per-actor pending count in the durable wake queue
guards.trigger: rows are pending for this actor and the session holds the fleet lock
guards.remedy: bin/fm-wake-drain.sh

guards.invariant: a Cursor primary never ends a turn with supervision off
guards.source: Cursor stop-hook park ownership, watcher beacon age, session identity
guards.trigger: the hook-owned park cannot establish a live cycle within its bounded attempts
guards.remedy: bin/fm-supervision-instructions.sh --repair-line (Cursor renders the stop-hook park remedy; restart cursor-agent so the park hook loads)

guards.invariant: firstmate-on-itself work never strands the primary checkout on a feature branch
guards.source: the named git branch of the code root versus the expected branch
guards.trigger: the code root is on a feature branch or detached HEAD while firstmate work runs
guards.remedy: git switch <expected-branch> in this code root

guards.invariant: a worker launch never targets the primary checkout
guards.source: git topology: worktree root, git dir, common dir, and the project clone
guards.trigger: the resolved launch target resolves to the primary checkout of the project
guards.remedy: bin/fm-spawn.sh <task> <project-clone> --mode <mode> --yolo <on|off> (a fresh spawn allocates its isolated copy through the treehouse lease; use bin/fm-control.sh <task> reassociate --worktree <replacement-copy> for an existing task)

guards.invariant: a dispatch refuses a brief whose Captain's intent or Firstmate spec is still a scaffold placeholder
guards.source: brief text of ## Captain's intent and ## Firstmate spec
guards.trigger: fm_brief_dispatch_problems finds an unfenced standalone scaffold token in its matching Task subsection
guards.remedy: edit <brief> and replace {TASK} and {FIRSTMATE_SPEC}; bin/fm-brief.sh <task> <repo> --mode <mode> scaffolds a complete brief

guards.invariant: a dispatch refuses a brief whose Definition of Done still holds scaffold tokens
guards.source: brief Definition Of Done section body or its DoD file
guards.trigger: any of the five DoD tokens remains in the section or the referenced file
guards.remedy: edit <brief> and fill the listed DoD tokens, or add an unfenced line 'DoD file: <absolute path>' to the section; bin/fm-brief.sh <task> <repo> --mode <mode> scaffolds the section

guards.invariant: a fresh dispatch refuses a brief whose scaffolded exclusion list is still blank
guards.source: brief text under ### Out of scope in # Task
guards.trigger: fm_brief_dispatch_problems finds a ### Out of scope heading in # Task with no stated exclusion
guards.remedy: edit <brief> and list the excluded work under ### Out of scope or write None; bin/fm-brief.sh <task> <repo> --mode <mode> scaffolds the heading

guards.invariant: a no-mistakes gate agent never drives the real fleet
guards.source: NO_MISTAKES_GATE env, git-common-dir under .no-mistakes/repos, lab-home marker
guards.trigger: the process is a gate agent and FM_HOME carries no lab marker
guards.remedy: eval "$(bin/fm-lab-home.sh env)" to mint the permitted lab home and export FM_HOME, then re-run the call (a real home is intentionally unavailable to a gate agent)

guards.invariant: a home without publication authority never pushes, opens a PR, or files an issue against firstmate upstream
guards.source: config/firstmate-role, inherited maintainer receipt, per-task upstream consent
guards.trigger: a publishing contract targets firstmate's own upstream and neither maintainer scope nor task consent names it
guards.remedy: captain grants config/firstmate-role with 'maintainer <host>/<owner>/<repo>', or records one-task consent as --upstream-consent <host>/<owner>/<repo> at dispatch

guards.invariant: a PR is never merged while a required check is red or has not reported at that head
guards.source: live forge PR state, check rollup at the exact head, required-check set for the base branch
guards.trigger: any unwaived required check at the current head is not green
guards.remedy: bin/fm-pr-merge.sh <task-id> <pr-url> --allow-red <check-name> for a non-green check, or --allow-missing <check-name> for a required check that never reported (both attended only); a pending check clears by re-running bin/fm-pr-merge.sh <task-id> <pr-url> once it reports

guards.invariant: an away session never waives a check or queues an unattended merge
guards.source: away-posture record, its lock, and live session ownership
guards.trigger: an away record exists and the merge asks for a waiver or an unattended merge
guards.remedy: return from away so the away record is archived, then bin/fm-pr-merge.sh <task-id> <pr-url> --allow-red <check-name> (attended only)

guards.invariant: a merge never runs while its task is still held for the captain
guards.source: bin/fm-captain-hold.sh open exit status for the task
guards.trigger: the task still has an open captain hold
guards.remedy: bin/fm-captain-hold.sh answer <task> --decision-file <captain-answer-file> --release

guards.invariant: a steer never resolves task targets against the wrong firstmate home
guards.source: presence and value of FM_HOME
guards.trigger: FM_HOME is unset or empty
guards.remedy: FM_HOME=<home> bin/fm-send.sh <task> <message>

guards.invariant: cleanup never discards uncommitted, unlanded, or unpushed work
guards.source: git status, forge PR merge state, PR head compared with local commits
guards.trigger: the copy holds uncommitted changes, or commits not proven present in a merged PR head
guards.remedy: land the work first: bin/fm-pr-merge.sh <pr>, or ask the captain for explicit discard authority and rerun bin/fm-teardown.sh <task> --force

guards.invariant: a worker never silently bills an Anthropic or third-party API instead of the subscription login
guards.source: ANTHROPIC_* variables in the environment and tmux session, plus the explicit --allow-api-key opt-in
guards.trigger: an API key or auth token is present in the launch environment without the opt-in
guards.remedy: env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN bin/fm-spawn.sh <task> ... (or pass --allow-api-key to bill the API deliberately)

guards.invariant: a launcher refuses an inherited credential that would silently bill an API
guards.source: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/AUTH_TOKEN in the inherited environment
guards.trigger: the harness would inherit an API credential with no explicit opt-in
guards.remedy: env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN <launcher>

guards.invariant: a launch never uses a profile picked from malformed rules or an unpermitted candidate
guards.source: config/crew-dispatch rules file, config/model-index.json, dispatch resolution
guards.trigger: the written brief resolves to a malformed rule, an ambiguous array, or an unauthorized candidate
guards.remedy: bin/fm-dispatch-resolve.sh <brief> prints the resolved profile or the exact malformed field to fix in config/crew-dispatch.json against config/model-index.json

guards.invariant: a persistent top-level cd never moves this session out of its home
guards.source: hook payload command string; git-dir versus git-common-dir of the destination
guards.trigger: a top-level cd, pushd, or popd would leave the home or the repository
guards.remedy: run the command in a subshell: ( cd <dir> && <command> ); bin/fm-cd-pretool-check.sh --command '<cmd>' reports the offending segment

guards.invariant: a watcher arm never runs backgrounded in the shell
guards.source: hook payload command string tokenized; harness backgrounding flags
guards.trigger: an arm or checkpoint invocation carries & or a backgrounding flag
guards.remedy: bin/fm-watch-checkpoint.sh --seconds <n> (foreground) or the harness-native arm tool named by bin/fm-supervision-instructions.sh --repair-line

guards.invariant: a fork-exhausting process tree never starves every other process on the host
guards.source: kernel PID count versus RLIMIT_NPROC or PID_MAX
guards.trigger: the PID census crosses the pressure line
guards.remedy: bin/fm-proc-guard.py check --json (prints the count, limit, percent, and verdict) and bin/fm-proc-guard.py census (writes the census with the top offenders and prints its path)

guards.invariant: host memory or swap pressure is never mistaken for a wedged worker
guards.source: macOS memory_pressure and sysctl, or /proc/meminfo
guards.trigger: memory or swap pressure crosses the audit's line
guards.remedy: bin/fm-mem-guard.py --json (prints the measured pressure and the verdict used by the recovery playbook)

guards.invariant: a malformed or partially marked Kimi config is never rewritten
guards.source: tomllib parse of $HOME/.kimi-code/config.toml and its region markers
guards.trigger: the Firstmate region markers are partial, duplicated, or altered
guards.remedy: repair the Firstmate region in $HOME/.kimi-code/config.toml by hand, then bin/fm-kimi-turnend-hook.sh install

guards.invariant: a write or edit action whose input cannot be validated or whose terminal audit record cannot be written never runs
guards.source: the write/edit tool input schema and the append to state/jev-guard.jsonl; write/edit content receives no Jev judgment
guards.trigger: write or edit content is not a string, or the terminal audit row cannot be appended
guards.remedy: replay the refusal with bin/fm-jev-guard-hook.sh <home> <config> <state> <task> <worktree> <data> <project> FIRSTMATE_JEV_GUARD_V1 < <payload> (prints the review reason and error type); the deny line already names the refused path

guards.invariant: a write without a proved filesystem target or proved local native-device effect is blocked
guards.source: bin/fm-jev-guard.ts deviceEffects and lspEffects tables, plain-path regex, repository roots, realpaths and session-owned running-job snapshot
guards.trigger: a filesystem target fails its path/root check, a device has no measured effect or fails its local scope proof, or a device is refused for its measured effect (xd://report_issue egress, xd://github unscreened results)
guards.remedy: for files use a plain absolute or worktree-relative path; for devices run read xd://<device> and report the refused device and intended effect to Firstmate for a measured rule in bin/fm-jev-guard.ts; local LSP calls other than status need an existing worktree file or a workspace symbols search (file "*"); for GitHub reads (repo_view, file_read) use gh-axi through the shell, and report every other GitHub op to Firstmate

guards.invariant: a captured Lavish reply is never left unhandled
guards.source: inbox markers: result present, no handled marker
guards.trigger: a Lavish result exists and no handling marker was written
guards.remedy: bin/fm-inbox.sh drain --ack <id> after handling the reply

guards.invariant: a launch never targets a backend that cannot hold a task endpoint
guards.source: static known-backend and spawn-supported tables plus live capability probe
guards.trigger: the resolved backend is unknown or not spawn-capable
guards.remedy: bin/fm-spawn.sh <task> <project> --mode <mode> --yolo <on|off> --backend <spawn-capable-backend>

guards.invariant: a turn that reports work as done names evidence the transcript or tests actually carry
guards.source: Belay model judgment over the Stop payload plus the completed-work evidence in the transcript
guards.trigger: the judgment finds a completion claim with no supporting evidence and the model answered
guards.proxy_reason: a model judgment is the only available judge for 'does this completion claim have evidence'; a deterministic source would be a citation parser the audit did not authorize
guards.remedy: state the evidence and rerun the turn: cite the file, command, or test output that proves the claim, or bin/fm-jev-belay-hook.sh < stop-payload replays the judgment for one payload
guards.exemptions_note: fail-open on a model outage is disclosed here, not silent

guards.invariant: a worker host tool with no row in the tool policy table never runs
guards.source: TOOL_POLICY in bin/fm-jev-egress.ts, keyed by the lower-cased host tool name
guards.trigger: toolPolicy(<tool>) finds no row for the called tool name, for example an MCP tool, a legacy MultiEdit or a newly added host tool
guards.remedy: report_issue and SendFeedback upload reports and must never receive a TOOL_POLICY row, so their refusal has no remedy; for every other <tool>, Firstmate adds a row to TOOL_POLICY in bin/fm-jev-egress.ts, classified by the tool's real effect, then runs bash tests/fm-jev-guard-audit.test.sh; the deny line names the tool and no call was made
guards.fail_direction_note: the table is compiled into the guard module; a runtime that cannot load it is denied in an active project scope and, per docs/configuration.md Jev guard, does not block in an inactive project scope
guards.telemetry_note: each allow and deny decision emits one event through bin/fm-guard-event.sh into state/guard-events.jsonl with the guard id, decision and elapsed time only, keyed to session <task>:<tool-name> so only a later allow of the same subject clears a deny; the content-free terminal row in state/jev-guard.jsonl remains the task audit

guards.invariant: a tool whose policy row names a destination class, or a memory operation whose local effect the live worker settings do not prove, never runs without a task grant for that class
guards.source: the tool's TOOL_POLICY row in bin/fm-jev-egress.ts; for a memory row, memoryEgress over the worker's live omp memory.backend, mnemopi.noEmbeddings and mnemopi.llmMode settings, read through omp's settings registry by the extension bin/fm-spawn.sh generates; plus the single egress= JSON line in state/<task>.meta; a skill-bearing learn retains its independently recorded T5 write owner even when its memory effect is refused
guards.trigger: egressClass(<tool>) returns a destination class, or memoryEgress(<tool>) names a model or remote call or an effect it could not prove local and so requires provider, and state/<task>.meta has no single valid egress= line listing that class: absent, malformed, duplicated, an unknown class, unreadable or symlinked
guards.remedy: Firstmate, never the worker, records exactly one grant line in state/<task>.meta, for example `printf 'egress=["<class>"]\n' >> state/<task>.meta` when none exists; the deny line names the missing class and no outbound call was made; a memory refusal also names the operation and the model call, remote call or local effect it could not prove
guards.fail_direction_note: an unreadable, malformed or symlinked grant record grants nothing; unreadable live memory settings, an unrecognized backend or llmMode, or embeddings left on prove nothing local, so the memory operation requires provider; the table is compiled into the guard module; a runtime that cannot load it is denied in an active project scope and, per docs/configuration.md Jev guard, does not block in an inactive project scope
guards.telemetry_note: each allow and deny decision emits one event through bin/fm-guard-event.sh into state/guard-events.jsonl with the guard id, decision, source_ok (task record readable) and elapsed time only, keyed to session <task>:<destination-class> so only a later allow of the same subject clears a deny; the content-free terminal row in state/jev-guard.jsonl remains the task audit

guards.invariant: an omp github call whose op is not one of omp's read ops never runs under any task grant
guards.source: the op argument of the github call, checked by refusedGithubOp in bin/fm-jev-egress.ts against the read ops installed omp 18.12.6 approves as reads (repo_view, file_read, search_issues, search_prs, search_code, search_commits, search_repos, run_watch)
guards.trigger: refusedGithubOp(<input>) finds a github op outside those read ops, such as pr_checkout, pr_create or pr_push, which write worktrees, branches, git config, refs or the remote, or an unknown, non-string or missing op
guards.remedy: no grant clears it; make the change with git and the no-mistakes pipeline (`no-mistakes axi run`), or read GitHub with `gh-axi` through the shell; the deny line names the op and no call was made
guards.fail_direction_note: an op that is missing, not a string or not a recognized read op is refused; the read-op list is compiled into the guard module; a runtime that cannot load it is denied in an active project scope and, per docs/configuration.md Jev guard, does not block in an inactive project scope
guards.telemetry_note: each github call emits one event through bin/fm-guard-event.sh into state/guard-events.jsonl with the guard id, decision (allow for a read op, deny for any other op), source_ok and elapsed time only, keyed to session <task>:github-read for an allow and <task>:github-write for a deny, so a read op never counts as clearing a write-op refusal, which nothing clears; a read op then still meets jev-egress-grant; the content-free terminal row in state/jev-guard.jsonl remains the task audit

guards.invariant: an omp worker's read, grep or ast-grep call never fetches a URL path
guards.source: omp's fetch.enabled setting, set false in .omp/fm-worker-overlay.yml, which bin/fm-spawn.sh passes to every omp ship and scout launch
guards.trigger: an omp worker calls read, grep or ast-grep with an http or https URL path
guards.remedy: use a web-classed tool under a task grant instead: Firstmate records egress=["web"] in state/<task>.meta and the worker calls web_search; omp's own error reads URL reads are disabled by settings.
guards.fail_direction_note: bin/fm-spawn.sh refuses an omp worker launch when .omp/fm-worker-overlay.yml is missing
guards.telemetry_note: not instrumented: this decision is omp's, not Firstmate's, and is visible only in the worker transcript; docs/guard-spec.md Rule 8 applies to Firstmate decision points

guards.invariant: a task commit never adds a line holding a known credential shape
guards.source: lines git diff --cached adds against HEAD and every MERGE_HEAD parent, after the repository pre-commit hook, net of lines the same diff removes, matched against the anchored shapes in bin/fm-git-secrets.py
guards.trigger: an added staged line holds a private-key header, a GitHub, AWS access key or Slack token prefix shape, or a connection URL with an embedded password of 8 or more characters
guards.remedy: remove the credential from the named files, restage them with git add <file>, and rerun git commit; python3 bin/fm-git-secrets.py pre-commit replays the check against the index
guards.layer_note: per-task wrappers installed by bin/fm-git-strip-ai-trailers.sh: pre-commit scans after the repository hook; pre-push scans before replaying the ref-update input to it. A refusal repeats only while the same new credential-shaped line, identified by its content hash, is refused in consecutive decisions. Different refused content starts at 1 even after an abandoned attempt; an allowed decision clears the counts. Each refusal past the budget of 1 also prints an escalation to a human decision, and the operation stays refused

guards.invariant: a task push never sends a commit that adds a line holding a known credential shape
guards.source: lines each outgoing commit adds against all of its parents, where outgoing means reachable from a pushed tip but from no advertised old tip and no remote-tracking ref, net of lines the same diff removes, matched against the anchored shapes in bin/fm-git-secrets.py
guards.trigger: an outgoing commit adds a line holding a private-key header, a GitHub, AWS access key or Slack token prefix shape, or a connection URL with an embedded password of 8 or more characters
guards.remedy: squash the outgoing commits that add the credential without it: git reset --soft <upstream>, remove the credential from the named files, restage them with git add <file>, git commit, then rerun git push; git log -p <upstream>..HEAD -- <file> shows the adding commits
guards.layer_note: per-task wrappers installed by bin/fm-git-strip-ai-trailers.sh: pre-commit scans after the repository hook; pre-push scans before replaying the ref-update input to it. A refusal repeats only while the same new credential-shaped line, identified by its content hash, is refused in consecutive decisions. Different refused content starts at 1 even after an abandoned attempt; an allowed decision clears the counts. Each refusal past the budget of 1 also prints an escalation to a human decision, and the operation stays refused
